Judith “Judy” Carol Counts Barker

August 1, 2026

    Sponsored by

    Judith “Judy” Carol Counts Barker, age 80, of Grayson, Kentucky, peacefully passed away with family at her bedside on July 11, 2026, at Elliott Nursing and Rehabilitation in Sandy Hook, Kentucky. Born on November 8, 1945, in Grayson, Judy was the beloved daughter of the late Cecil Clyde and Dexter Marie Brown Counts. She was preceded in death by her husband Ralph Eugene Barker; her infant daughter, Lesa Fawn Barker; her son, Pride Eugene Barker; and her brother, Roger Counts.

    Judy was a dedicated homemaker who poured her heart into nurturing her family. She was curious, an avid reader, horseback rider and hiker in her younger years and loved colorful clothes, glasses in windows and sparkly things.  She played the piano, especially loving the tunes of gospel songs.  She was no stranger to manual labor, using hand sickle, sprouting hoe and cross saw to clear weeds, brush and trees.  She and her husband Ralph lived in a log cabin until they built their own home with the help of family and friends.  She hung laundry on the clothes line with bleach reddened hands while singing up a storm. She did not use TV or technology, but kept up with the world and local events from her daily five minutes of radio news.  Judy was all about “social media” before it was a thing—she proudly touted her children’s accomplishments and all about the family’s trips, visitors, and reunions in the pages of the Grayson newspaper which she fondly called “the Grayson Tattler!” She was known by the family as “The Dispatcher”, and was better than any GPS or geo-tracker, always knowing where everyone was, what they were doing and then sharing with the family this information of the whereabouts and activities of those whom she loved. Bargain shopping was her joy.  She loved haggling with flea market folks, having gotten her horse trading characteristics from her Dad Cecil.  She enjoyed yard sales, flea markets, thrift stores and was usually first in line at “Marie’s” on Thursdays. She knew good quality and loved being on the hunt for items that her friends or family were searching for, then often generously giving them as gifts.  She believed in supporting the local community and businesses.  She kept an eye out for shoe sales at Rupert’s and kept her kids and grandkids shod, choosing to spend her savings on them rather than herself.  She taught her children good values, life skills, the importance of education, and to save for a rainy day.  She helped them at very young ages to open their savings accounts with the Commercial Bank, making a big production of them going to deposit even $1 or $2, get a free lollipop and to wave at Fred Buck.  She made her children do their homework and helped them study for tests, pressing them to excel.  She commanded they do their chores and did not tolerate laziness.  She did not allow littering and enlisted her kids to pick up garbage along Maddox Trail, teaching that you give back to the community in which you reside.   She loved watching wildlife on her home place, and cherished the simple joys of life, particularly the wildflowers her dear children brought her during their visits, symbolizing the love and connection they shared. Her warm spirit and kind heart left an indelible mark on everyone she met.

    Advertisement

    Judy is survived by her two daughters, Angela Barker Thomas of Grayson (and Angela’s Thomas stepfamilies in Alabama and Colorado); Crystal (Rosalinda) Barker of Las Vegas, NV; a son, Lad Ralph Barker of Grayson, KY; granddaughter Katie “Sunny” Barker; and grandsons Jacob (Devyn), Eren (Kassie), and Braxton Barker who will carry forward her legacy. She is also survived by two sisters, Myrtle Counts Suttles of Grayson and Jean (John) Counts Bush of Gallipolis Ferry, WV, along with a host of friends and extended family who will deeply miss her presence.

    A private committal service was held at the Sabra Carroll Cemetery, located at the intersection of Maddox Trail and Barker Drive.  A  celebration of life to honor Judy will be held at the Grayson Lake Dam Shelter #4 (near the Spillway) on October 25, 2026 from 1pm – 3pm, with a country lunch to be served featuring a few of Mom’s favorite foods. 

    The Barker family would like to express special thanks to her sister Jean for faithful cards and correspondence; sister Myrtle for her many calls and help through hard times; cousin Bruce Everman for calls and visits at the nursing home; cousins Larry and Gayle Knipp and neighbors Larry and Betty Scaggs for visits and keeping her in summer vegetables and eggs; Sue Mullins for her calls; the Kirklands for their cards and visits; Camila Haney for cards and visits; her faith community of Wolf Creek Baptist Church; and to her health care team members of Pathways of Grayson, Eastern State Hospital, King’s Daughters Hospital and clinic, St. Claire Regional Medical Center, Community Hospice, and Elliott Nursing and Rehabilitation for their support, care and kindness throughout the years.

    The Malone Funeral Home in Grayson managed all services for the Barker family. Condolences may be sent to the family at www.malonefuneralhome.com.  In lieu of flowers, the family requests calls, cards or texts of support in the following weeks.

    Judy Barker’s loving spirit and her dedication to her family and friends will be remembered fondly by all who knew her.
